full_judgment:
Mr. A. K. Badrul Huq, J:- A Judgment of volte face recorded by learned Appellate Judge in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 1999 overruling rendered by learned trail judge in Miscellaneous Case no. 4 of 1989 laid under section 96 of State Acquisition and tenancy Act (For short the Act) dismissing Miscellaneous case is under protest in this Civil Revision Petition under section 115 of the case of Civil Procedure Briefly the code). 

 ii) Sonabuddin Saial had been the owner of 1.45 acres of land recorded in State Acquisition Khatian No. 81. On the death of Sonabuddin Saial, his son Hossain Ali Saial and daughter Tufani Bibi along with other heir son and daughter inherited land left by Sonabuddin saial. Pre-emptor First opposite party because co-sharer by purchase over 17-1/2 + 3-1/2 in all 21 acreas of land on the strength of two deeds of conveyance dated 31.7.1991 and 17.12.1991 respectively from heir son Hossain Ali Saial and daughter Tufani Bibi of Sonabuddin Saial. 

 11. Another legal decrepitude and inherent disability is demonstrated in the Agreement itself and this disorder and disablement strikes at the root of the Agreement. Section 95A of The Act ordains that any transfer of a holding or of a portion or share-thereof, either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to re-convey or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess and to enjoy the usufruct of such holding or portion or share thereof for a specified period in lieu of such consideration shall be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provision of section 95 of The Act shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement to State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (Second Amendment) Order, 1972. 

 18. In this context it is profitable to state that right of pre-emption is not an absolute right and the same is subject to any Agreement accompanying the sale. If the right of pre-emption is enforced with the notice of Agreement, the Pre-emptor takes the land/property subject to Agreement. 

 20. Exploration of the Judgment passed by learned senior Judge indicates that the learned judge failed to notice the tenor of section 95A and section 96 (10) (b) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and committed an error of law and by the error the merit of the adjudication of the case had been seriously affected. Judgment perilously borders perversity and legal infirmity. On the other hand learned sub-ordinate Judge as the Appellate Judge approached the debate in correct direction and reversing decision rendered by him is well founded and well merited. 

 22. Decisions of facts reached by Appellate Judge as last and final Judge of fact based on evidence and materials on record are not open to interference by High Court Division in exercise of revisional jurisdiction contemplated in section 115 of the Code. unless it is shown that decision are based upon gross misreading of evidence those has been founded on misconception or misapplication or misapprehension of law or any misinterpretation of any material document or otherwise those are perverse being contrary to law, evidences and materials on record. Support for this proposition is sought to be drawn from a series of decisions both of Our Jurisdiction and Foreign Jurisdiction. Durga Choudhrain Vs. Jawahir Singh, 17 Indian Appeal 122, Nefar Chandra Pal Chowdhury Vs. Shukkur Sheikh, AIR 1918 P.0 92 Ramchandra Vs. Ray Lingam AIR 1963 SC 302 Fokaruddin iVlia and another Vs. Mohammad Khoda Baksu Sheikh, 29 DLR (SC) 268. Akrab Ali Vs. Zaihiruddin, 30 DLR (SC) 81. Abdul Mann. Chowdhury, Vs. Chapala Rani Sen and others, 37 DLR (AD) 205, Naimuddin Sardar Vs., Md. Abdul Kalam, 41 DLR (AD) 3, Jasimuddin Kanchan Vs. Ali Ashraf, 42 DLR (AD) 289, Mazharul Borhan Vs. A.H. Bhuiyan, 15 BLD (AD) 237 and Haider Unnessa and another Vs. Monwara Begum and other 10 BLD (AD) 280, Federal Radid Commission Vs. Nelson Brothers Board and Electric and Power Company Vs. National Relations Board, (1942) 319 U.S. 533, Gujt Heluering Commissioner of Internationals. Revenue Vs. John Kehoc, (1939) 309 U.S. 267 and State of New York and others Vs. United States of America (1946) 331 U.S 284 are some of the authorities which may be profitably noticed. A study of the decision rendered, reason assigned in rendering decision and conclusion reached by Appellate Judge does not come into sight that there had been misreading of evidence or those had been founded on any misconception, misapplication and misapprehension of law or mis-interpretation of any material document or otherwise those were wrong headed. On bestowing my anxious and dispassionate consideration and thought and having also taken into account of all the pros and cons of the matter and the catena of authorities pronounced by Superior courts of our Jurisdiction and also of foreign Jurisdiction I am of this conviction that this Rule arising out of Civil Revision Potion is bereft of any substance and the same must be discharged.
